title: Workspace
description: A folder agents work in, in a container of its own: the folder, and the container's CPUs and memory.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: The kind and version this file is written in; always its first field.

title.description: The name clients show for this record; the file's own name when empty.
title.title: Title

path.description: The folder on this machine; its container sees it as /workspace, and nothing else of the machine.
path.title: Folder

cpus.description: The CPUs its container may use; empty: half of what Docker has.
cpus.title: CPUs

memory_mib.description: The memory its container may use, in MiB; empty: a quarter of what Docker has.
memory_mib.title: Memory

layers.description: What its container has besides Clank's sandbox image, each built on it once: tex (TeX Live, for the LaTeX the agent writes, design 0020). Its container moves to the new image when it is next made.
layers.title: Image layers

setup.description: The command that installs the folder's own software into its home (~/.venv), run by Clank in a container that reaches the internet; empty: proposed from the folder's files (pyproject.toml, requirements.txt).
setup.title: Setup

set_up.description: The setup command that last ran to its end; empty: the software is not installed.
set_up.title: Installed with

mcp_allowed.description: The folder's own MCP servers (its .mcp.json) its agent gets, each with the fingerprint of its entry as allowed: an entry changed since is not given until it is allowed again.
mcp_allowed.title: Folder's MCP servers allowed

mcp_off.description: Your own MCP servers (clank mcp add) this workspace's agent does not get; the others it gets.
mcp_off.title: Your MCP servers held back

hosts.description: The internet hosts its agent reaches through Clank's proxy (design 0024): a name (pypi.org) or a suffix (.arxiv.org: arxiv.org and every name under it), each with when and how it was allowed. Every other host is refused; private addresses always.
hosts.title: Hosts its agent may reach

changes.description: review: the agent asks before it changes a file, and you accept or reject the change (VS Code shows it beside your files); auto: it changes files without asking, and VS Code shows each change after.
changes.title: The agent's changes

one_window.description: Opening OpenCode in a terminal (VS Code's, or the console's) first closes every OpenCode window open in the workspace, so there is only ever one and switching between plan, review and auto reaches it; off: each opening adds another window. OpenCode without a terminal (the phone's) is left alone.
one_window.title: One OpenCode window

models.description: this-machine: its agent's requests go only to a model on this machine; cloud: also to a cloud model, once you allowed it (design 0016 §9). Every workspace starts on this machine.
models.title: Where its requests may go

cloud_answered.description: When you last answered whether it may use the cloud model; empty: never asked, or not answered in time, so it is asked the next time a cloud model would serve it.
cloud_answered.title: Cloud answered
